body: Before astronauts return to the lunar surface, NASA will first conduct one of the most ambitious and complex test missions in the agency’s history.  Launching in 2027, Artemis III will send NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, Andre Douglas, and ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano aboard the Orion spacecraft into low Earth orbit to perform a series of demonstrations with test versions, or test articles, of human landing systems being developed by industry partners Blue Origin and SpaceX. During the planned 14-day mission, crews and flight controllers will practice the rendezvous, docking, habitation, and operational procedures that will be essential when Artemis astronauts begin landing near the Moon’s South Pole in 2028. title: Not a fan of full-screen Calling Cards? Keep an eye out for this update
summary: Google's working on a 'compact' option for Calling Card images.
body: TL;DR Google is working on a new Compact Photo option for Calling Cards in its Phone app. The option could let users display smaller contact photos instead of full-screen images. Four color presets have surfaced, potentially allowing users to customize the background behind these smaller photos. The feature isn’t functional yet. One of the Google Phone app ‘s coolest additions may have started out as a bit of a copy of Apple’s Contact Posters , but an upcoming option could help Google differentiate its implementation. The feature I’m talking about is Calling Cards , and it looks like Google wants to give users more flexibility over how they appear on your phone’s screen. Up until now, Calling Cards have appeared as full-screen images whenever a contact you’ve assigned an image to calls you — same as how Apple’s version works. But not everyone wants a huge image filling their phone’s entire screen every time someone calls. That’s what Google appears to be addressing.

title: Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreak discovery could open the door to a world of mods
summary: An obscure game has provided an unlikely route into Nintendo's latest console.
body: Credit: Pepsipu.com TL;DR A developer has released a software-only Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreak that works on the latest firmware. The exploit uses vulnerabilities involving SmileBASIC 4 and has already been demonstrated with Mario Kart World mods. The jailbreak isn’t permanent and doesn’t yet provide full control over the console. Unsurprisingly, Nintendo hasn’t exactly made life easy for anyone hoping to tinker with the Switch 2 beyond its intended limits. But one developer has now made a significant breakthrough, releasing a software-only Switch 2 jailbreak that works even on the console’s latest firmware. Security researcher Sammy Hajhamid, who goes by pepsipu online, announced the achievement on X and explained how it works in a detailed blog post . The exploit, called ns2jb, works on firmware version 23.0.1 without requiring any physical modifications to the console. There are caveats, but the jailbreak may open the door to things like unofficial software and game modifications.

title: Some Android phones and Google Calendar events could soon be an hour off
summary: Android users in parts of Canada should check their phones before November 1.
body: TL;DR Parts of Canada are switching to permanent daylight saving time on November 1, ending seasonal clock changes. Google warns that Android phones running outdated software could incorrectly turn their clocks back by an hour. Some Google Calendar events could also shift by an hour, with certain appointments requiring manual corrections through the web version. The biannual tradition of changing clocks is coming to an end for a subset of the Canadian population, though with that convenience comes an added side of initial headaches. Permanent daylight saving time for British Columbia, Alberta, Manitoba, and the Northwest Territories starts on November 1, and with the date just a little over a week away at this point, Google wants to help Android users in those regions — or anyone traveling through them — make the transition. If the new rule hadn’t gone into effect, clocks in those regions would automatically turn back by an hour. Starting November 1, however, that won’t happen. While that sounds like a seamless transition, there’s a big catch here, especially for users who haven’t updated their Android devices.

Is there any relationship between a streaming service and its users that’s more contentious than YouTube’s? Even putting the interminable struggle between YouTube and ad blockers aside for the moment, it feels like nearly every single change the service makes to its interface is met with fierce pushback . Earlier this week, we told you about the newest controversy, as some viewers reported that the dislike button in videos was being hidden away , out of reach.
